title: Zephyrine and the Songbook
premise: Noor Yarrow, a once-celebrated cellist who froze mid-concert and never played publicly again, retreats to the Provençal vineyard they inherited from a grandmother they barely knew, cataloguing her belongings before selling. Among her effects they find an unsent letter from eleven years ago—written by their first love, Zephyrine Aubert, and intercepted by Noor's controlling mentor—which reveals that Noor's 'catastrophic' collapse was engineered to keep them dependent. As harvest season ripens, Noor must decide whether to sell the vineyard and return to the gilded cage of their career, or stay, rebuild, and finally let Zephyrine—who has arrived as the estate's new consulting vintner—be seen clearly at last.
about_author: Beatrix Joubert is a former orchestral librarian turned novelist who writes about music, memory, and the families we choose. She lives between Lyon and a small olive farm, where she keeps her grandmother's recipe notebook open on the kitchen counter.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback to the catastrophic final performance: mid-cadenza, Noor's hands simply stop, and the hall's silence becomes permanent. Present day: Noor arrives at the neglected vineyard, telling themselves the heart is trainable muscle. Emotional beat: numb self-protection masking grief.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Cataloguing Grand-mère Odile's house, Noor finds sheet music annotated in two hands—one their own, from childhood visits they'd suppressed. The lawyer mentions the estate is solvent only if the harvest comes in. Beat: unease; the past is closer than claimed.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Inside a hollowed songbook, Noor discovers Zephyrine's unsent love letter, yellowed, pleading, unanswered for over a decade. The postmark date is three days before the collapse. Beat: vertigo—the foundation of Noor's whole narrative cracks.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Knew
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In Lyon, cellist-turned-teacher Zephyrine receives a call about consulting work at the Yarrow vineyard—and recognizes the name instantly. She has spent eleven years believing she was rejected. Beat: quiet fury and hope braided together.

chapters.title: The Consulting Vintner
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Zephyrine arrives at the vineyard; the reunion is polite, glacial, devastating. Neither admits knowledge of the letter. Beat: charged avoidance, two people performing composure.

chapters.title: Rows and Rows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Working the vines side by side, Zephyrine tests Noor with small provocations, watching for the person she loved beneath the armor. Noor almost laughs—for the first time in years. Beat: reluctant warmth.

chapters.title: Cello in a Dry Cellar
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor uncovers Odile's old cello in the cellar and, alone at midnight, plays four bars before stopping, shaking. Zephyrine hears from the stairs and says nothing. Beat: the body remembers what the mind forbids.

chapters.title: Marguerite Vasseur's Masterclass
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashbacks deepen: how mentor Marguerite shaped Noor's career, isolated them, framed devotion as discipline. Present-day Marguerite calls, pressing Noor to sign with her new foundation. Beat: the cage revealed as velvet.

chapters.title: First Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The village gathers for the harvest festival; Zephyrine watches Noor be welcomed by people who knew Odile, belonging arriving unasked. A near-kiss under lanterns is interrupted by a phone buzzing: Marguerite. Beat: longing against intrusion.

chapters.title: The Letter, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Drunk on festival wine, Noor confesses finding the letter—but claims not to know who wrote it. Zephyrine goes white and leaves. Beat: cowardice costs; guilt lands hard.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the ledger, Noor finds records showing Marguerite visited the vineyard eleven years ago—and paid the postal clerk to hold outgoing mail. The interception was deliberate. Beat: cold clarity; rage begins.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Press House
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine confronts Noor: why claim ignorance? Noor, terrified, deflects. Zephyrine decides to finish the harvest contract and go. Beat: heartbreak sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Phone Call, Recorded
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor calls Marguerite, fishing; Marguerite's denials are too fluent, and she lets slip details only the letter's contents could supply. Noor records it. Beat: the hunted turns hunter.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Wrong Weather
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine's own flashback: the years after the silence—dropped auditions, lost scholarships, all quietly arranged by Marguerite to punish her proximity to Noor. Beat: shared victimhood realized; grief for stolen time.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Vines
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleaved. A hailstorm threatens the crop days before harvest; Noor and Zephyrine fight to save it through the night, soaked and laughing and finally honest about everything except the letter. Beat: intimacy forged in crisis.

chapters.title: The Recording Goes Out
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor sends the recording to Marguerite's board and the press, then tells Zephyrine the truth: the letter was hidden, the collapse engineered, the silence bought. Zephyrine doesn't forgive—yet. Beat: exposure as liberation and risk.

chapters.title: Marguerite Arrives
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Marguerite descends on the vineyard, silk and sympathy, offering Noor a comeback tour and offering Zephyrine a settlement to disappear again. She nearly succeeds—until Odile's neighbors arrive, witnesses to that long-ago visit. Beat: power meeting its match.

chapters.title: The Songbook's Last Page
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the songbook's binding, Noor finds Odile's own letter: she knew what Marguerite did, hid the evidence, and left the vineyard to Noor hoping they'd come home to find it. Beat: inheritance redefined—not property, but truth.

chapters.title: Public, At Last
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the harvest festival's closing concert, Noor takes the stage in the village square, hands steady, and plays Odile's cello to a crowd of farmers. The muscle trains; the heart opens. Beat: catharsis; the wound answered.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Decides
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Offered a prestigious post back in Lyon, Zephyrine weighs eleven years of grievance against one season of honesty. She stays through the crush, but won't say yes to anything more yet. Beat: earned caution; love without surrender.

chapters.title: Vendange
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Harvest day: the whole village picks, presses, and celebrates; the first bottles are labeled with Odile's name. Noor signs papers keeping the vineyard, declining Marguerite's tour permanently. Beat: rootedness chosen over spectacle.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Noor and Zephyrine alternate final pages. On the cellar steps, Noor plays; Zephyrine sings the melody the letter once quoted. They begin again—slowly, truthfully—with the year's first wine between them. Beat: resolution; belonging and love, finally unhidden.
